consequences: Producers must publish schema-versioned events; breaking schema changes require a new version, not an edit.
The team owns and operates an event bus — new on-call surface, with runbooks before launch.
Batch ingestion is retained as a backfill path, so both paths must be tested on every schema change.
Creators see numbers within minutes, which raises the bar on data-quality monitoring.
context: Northlight Studios (sample data — fictional) runs a Creator Analytics pipeline that ingests playback and payout events in nightly batches. Creators see yesterday's numbers at best, and support gets the same question every morning: "where are my numbers?" Batch windows are also getting longer as the catalog grows, so the 6-hour lag is trending worse, not better.
decision: Move ingestion to an event-driven model: producers publish schema-versioned events to a central event bus, and the analytics pipeline consumes them in near real time. Batch ingestion stays as a backfill path only.
title: Adopt event-driven ingestion for the Creator Analytics pipeline
